Note: this isn't based on any studies or clinical backing. I came up with this on my own through personal inspection.

NARE

Basically, people get used to something and can not extract themselves from all the entanglements (like quantum physics) that get associated with it.

My example: everybody told me my X was off (not retarded off) and I just kept trying to apply more love and hope under the idea she'd come around. It took mountain moving effort to break away and and universe shattering realization that I was fucked up from way earlier than I thought. I spent a long time, trying to figure out why I stayed around for so long even knowing that my relationship was beyond broken.

This can apply to all kinds of situations, like staying at a job, addiction, or even keeping company with people that you call friends.

I ended up calling it NARE based on the Japanese word because it also has connotations of being more than getting used to something.

When you enter the zone of NARE everything is normal and those around you are wrong. Also, you look for ways to prove your sanity and to prove your world as gospel. You might turn to religion or find ways to prove that breaking away from what is breaking you isn't what you want -- which is to stay in that situation. Your friends and family are also wrong.

How do you break it? Well, how do break a habit or stop doing something that is second nature? Like I said earlier, it's a huge problem. It takes a life changing event or a huge amount of will power.

Because humans prefer the state of NARE, it's always easy to return to that death sentence. You have lived it before and since you didn't obviously die, it's not all that bad. I'd surmise that some people actively search out another situation that will end the same way because that is what's easiest. It's hard to break the habit of NARE.

The best hope is to form a new habit that is better than the one you just got out of. I look at my new wife as a better habit -- it's obviously a way healthier relationship, yet, I see NARE here too. Some of my old habits still exist but at least they are the less damaging ones.

Even if you attainted Buddhahood, you still have NARE because it's one of the fee immutable states yet one that you can at least make better with breaking away from all the bad habits.
NARE, what it is, the dangers of it and hopefully how to overcome it. Understanding NARE should at least shed some light on your situation.
